stem: A word is coded letter by letter under these rules, with the alphabet treated as a cycle so that z wraps to a. A letter at an odd position (1st, 3rd, 5th) moves forward 2 places. A letter at an even position (2nd, 4th) moves backward 1 place. But if the original letter is a vowel, it is instead replaced by the next vowel in the cycle a, e, i, o, u, a, whatever its position. Under these rules, what is the code for CHAIR?

per_option_rationale.rationale: EGCHT ignores the vowel override and shifts A and I by position instead. A at position 3 forward 2 gives C and I at position 4 back 1 gives H, but the vowel rule says A becomes E and I becomes O, so the third and fourth letters are wrong.

C at position 1 forward 2 is E. H at position 2 back 1 is G. A is a vowel, so it becomes the next vowel E. I is a vowel, so it becomes the next vowel O. R at position 5 forward 2 is T. The code is E G E O T.
BJEOQ swaps the position shifts, moving odd positions back 1 and even positions forward 2. C back 1 is B, H forward 2 is J, R back 1 is Q, which reverses the rule for the consonants.
EGUET takes the previous vowel rather than the next. A back one vowel is U and I back one vowel is E, but the rule advances to the next vowel, so A becomes E and I becomes O.

explanation: Apply the rules letter by letter to CHAIR. Position 1 C is an odd-position consonant, forward 2 gives E. Position 2 H is an even-position consonant, back 1 gives G. Position 3 A is a vowel, so the vowel rule overrides the position shift and A becomes the next vowel E. Position 4 I is a vowel, so I becomes the next vowel O. Position 5 R is an odd-position consonant, forward 2 gives T. Concatenating gives E G E O T.

explanation_sections.punchline: The vowel override is the cracker: A and I are vowels, so they advance to E and O regardless of position, giving EGEOT.
explanation_sections.approach: Number the letters of CHAIR 1 to 5 and check each against the rule hierarchy: vowel first, else odd-position forward 2, else even-position back 1. C odd to E, H even to G, A vowel to E, I vowel to O, R odd to T. The vowel rule must be tested before the position rule, since it overrides. Read off EGEOT and re-check the wrap-around was not needed here.
explanation_sections.lesson: When coding rules are conditional, fix the precedence first; an override like the vowel rule must be applied before the default position shift.
explanation_sections.timing: About 165 seconds. Fastest elimination is option (1) EGCHT: it shifts the vowels A and I by position, which the vowel override forbids, so it falls at the third letter.
